newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai PM sees mild economic recovery soon.
newsitem.headline: Thai PM sees mild economic recovery soon.

text.p: Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh said on Wednesday that his government expected a mild economic recovery in 1998 after suffering its worst economic crisis in a decade.

Chavalit told a parliamentary debate on the 1997/1998 (October/September) fiscal budget that the Thai gross domestic product would likely expand 5.7 percent in 1998 against revised, expected 5.6 percent growth this year.
The central bank has scaled down its 1997 GDP growth projection several times this year, to 5.9 percent last month from 7.1 percent early this year and against 6.4 percent in 1996.

"The economic slowdown has made it very tough for the government to propose a (balanced, deficit-free) budget... I believe the (1997/1998) austerity budget is appropriate under current economic and bearish financial sector conditions in the country," Chavalit said in his budget statement.

The government proposed to parliament a trimmed 982 billion baht ($39.3 billion) budget next year, a small four percent rise from this year. The planned expenditure is 26.59 billion baht lower than what it hoped to spend earier.
Thailand is facing its first budget deficit in a decade due to a sharp reduction in tax revenue caused by the economic slowdown.
The prime minister said inflation would likely ease to 4.4 percent in 1998 from 4.5 this year while the current account deficit would also narrow to 5.3 percent of GDP from 6.5 percent.

Chavalit said the Thai economic slowdown since 1996 and problems faced by property and financial sectors prompted the government to curb its 1997/1998 spending without sacrificing long-term development needs.

Opposition leader Chuan Leekpai responded to Chavalit's budget statement saying that the government tried to mislead the public by presenting a spending plan that could not be realistically financed by sharply declining tax revenue.
